texts.preamble: Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Kabc020312772021 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru. Dated This The 12th Day Of December 2024 Present: Sri.Kumara.S (B.A., Ll.B) Vii Addl. Scj and Acjm, Member, Mact-3, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.5337/2021 Petitioner : Sri.Malleshappa, S/o Basappa, Aged about 50 years, R/at 1st Floor, Krishnareddy Layout, Konappana Agrahara, Electronic City, Bengaluru - 560 100. Permanent Address: Yellambalase Village, Kaduru Taluk, Chikkamagalur District. (By Sri.H.T.Nataraj, Advocate) V/s Respondents : 01. The Managing Director, Ksrtc, K.H. Road, (Scch-3) 2 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 Shanthi Nagar, Bengaluru - 560 027. (By Smt.B.J.Suneetha, Advocate) 02. Internal Insurance Fund, Ksrtc, K.H. Road, Shanthinagar, Bengaluru - 560 027. (Exparte) Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/ 1 03. Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Company Ltd., Rep. by its Manager, # 25/3, 2nd Floor, Building No.2, Shankaranarayana Building, M.G. Road, Bangalore - 01. (By Sri.Kiran Pujar, Advocate) 04 . Sri.
texts.facts: This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident. 02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: On 21.09.2020 at about 12.45 a.m, when the petitioner was travelling in KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA- 42-F-1827 as passenger from Bengaluru to Kaduru, when it was proceeding at NH-206, near Prakruthi Daba, Nittur, Gadde Bayalu, at that time the driver of KSRTC Bus drove the bus in rash and negligent manner, with high speed and hit the parked Lorry (Tipper) bearing No.KA-52-A-1377 to its backside. Due to this the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries. Immediately after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Gubbi Government hospital, Tumakuru District, wherein after first aid he was shifted to Vijayanagar hospital, Bengaluru and admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and further went to HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru, for further better treatment and took treatment on OPD basis and once again admitted to same hospital as inpatient and has (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 undergone surgery. The petitioner has spent more than Rs.10,00,000/- towards hospital and medical expenses and Rs.1,00,000/- towards food, fruits, nourishment, conveyance and attendant charges and respondent No.1 has paid Rs.4,00,000/- towards his medical expenses directly to the Vijayanagar hospital on 09.10.2020 by way of cheque and except the said amount, the petitioner Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/ 2 has not received any amount and the remaining expenses was borne by the petitioner alone. The petitioner prior to accident was hale and healthy and was aged about 50 years and doing business of selling tender coconut in Bengaluru and earning Rs.2,000/- per day. Due to the accident he is not able to do his business and hence, he was unemployed and facing lot of financial crisis. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of KSRTC Bus and negligent parking of Tipper Lorry. Even a criminal case is registered against the said drivers of KSRTC Bus and Tipper Lorry. The respondents No.1 and 2 are the owner and internal insurer of KSRTC Bus and respondents No.3 and 4 are the insurer and owner of the Tipper Lorry, all are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- to the petitioner together with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs. (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 3 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed written statement. Inspite of service of notice, the respondents No.2 and 4 did not appeared and hence, they were placed exparte. 04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denies that there was any rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the K.S.R.T.C Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 and alleged accident and as a consequence of which the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and further contended that the bus was on its schedule trip from Bangalore to Shivamogga and the bus was being driven by its driver slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations and while it was so proceeding near Prakruthi Daba, Nittur Gaddebayalu. at about 1.15 a.m, a Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-l377 was so parked due to mechanical defect in the middle of the road, without displaying any signal and there was raining and when the things stood thus, a private bus was coming from the opposite side, with bright light and due to bright from the opposite side, tipper lorry was not visible till the bus reached near the tipper lorry. When the driver (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 of the bus noticed the tipper lorry stopped in the middle of the road without parking light, immediately stopped the bus and in that process it came in contact with the said tipper lorry. The tipper lorry had no parking lights nor reflectors fitted, further no warning devices were fitted to the vehicle and no top lights on the rear side of the parked vehicle and no road barricade was put around the tipper lorry. The unattended tipper lorry was so left in the dark night and it was parked in the middle of the road negligently, in flagrant violation of the traffic rules and regulations. As such for the alleged accident the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-l377 was wholly and solely responsible. But neither the bus in question not its driver responsible for the accident. However, the petitioner with an sole intention to make a wrongful gain from this respondent also, falsely implicated the bus in question and foisted a false case against this respondent and further Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/ 3 contended that this respondent immediately after the accident has paid a sum of Rs.14,54,004/- to the petitioner towards medical expenses as an ex-gratia. If this Court was pass an award and Judgment against this respondent, the aforesaid amount kindly be deducted in the Judgment and award. If this Court holds (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 contributory or sole negligence of lorry driver, in that case the respondents No 3 and 4 shall be directed to refund medical expenses of Rs.14,54,004/- paid by this respondent to the petitioner. The accident took place due to the negligence of the driver of the tipper lorry by parking the lorry in the middle of the road negligently in flagrant violation of traffic rules and regulations. But colluding with the Police the petitioner has got the case registered as against the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 to make the claim and enrich himself unlawfully and has further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of the KSRTC Bus, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1. 05. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Lorry bearing No.KA-52-A-1377 and liability to indemnify the respondent No.4 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the Bus bearing No.KA-42-F-1827 was solely responsible for (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 the accident, who hit the Lorry bearing No. KA-52-A-1377 from behind, infact the driver of the Lorry was no way responsible for the injuries and the driver of the Lorry was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and further was not qualified for holding or obtaining such driving licence and the vehicle was plying without having valid Permit as on the date of accident, thereby, the owner of the vehicle committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and this respondent denies the occurrence and mode of the accident and also actionable negligence of Lorry bearing No. KA-52-A-1377 and also denies manner and occurrence of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, age, occupation, income of the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner. The compensation claimed is exorbitant. Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.3. 06. 07. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined three witnesses as PW.2 to 4 and through them got marked 25 documents as Ex.P.1 to 25 and closed the petitioner side evidence. The Senior Manager of the respondent No.3 Insurance Company, the Driver and the Accounts Supervisor of the respondents No.1 and 2 Corporation got examined as RW.1 to 3 and got marked 10 documents as Ex.R.1 to 10 and closed their side evidence. During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.3 counsel he stated that he cannot say the width of accident road, but there was space for movement of one bus and even lorry was parked by the side of road and admits that the if the KSRTC bus proceed slowly then the accident could not taken place and eventhough there is sufficient space on the other side of road, the KSRTC bus had with rash driving dashed to the parked lorry and that the accident took place due to negligence of KSRTC bus driver and there was no negligence on the part of lorry. Further, PW.2 is MRO at HOSMAT hospital, Bengaluru and she has produced Ex.P.21 X-ray films and Ex.P.22 Inpatient records of petitioner. During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.3 counsel she stated that she do not know about the contents of documents produced and she do not know the doctor who treated the petitioner. Further, PW.3 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained open fracture both bones of LT leg type I and open fracture both bones of RT leg type IIIA and he assessed permanent partial impairment of both lower limbs at 57% and whole body impairment at 19% and he has (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 produced Outpatient record and X-rays as per Ex.P.23 and 24. During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.3 counsel he admits that when the petitioner was discharged from hospital his condition was stable and petitioner was admitted for the first time in their hospital on 19.07.2021 and that the petitioner when admitted on 19.07.2021 he was treated for infection in the right leg. Prior to their hospital the petitioner was took treatment at Vijayanagar hospital and that the petitioner was admitted in their hospital for second time for removal of external fixation at right leg and petitioner was suffering from diabetic and petitioner had took treatment only to his right leg in their hospital and admits that as per Ex.P.8 it is stated that the petitioner had sustained injuries to left leg. Now the right side implants are removed and the left side implants are in-situ and also admits that the petitioner required future medical intervention for removing left tibia nail and now the wounds are healed-up and petitioner has sustained upper leg fracture on right leg and middle leg fracture on left leg and the hip movements are normal and he has not issued estimation for future medical expenses (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 and admits that the petitioner has not sustained any amputation and admits that for aged person there will be problem of arthritis and also admits that as the petitioner is suffering from diabetics normally the healing of wounds will take time and he has assessed only physical disability and he has not issued any disability certificate and fractures are united and there was a considerable improvements and with some difficulties petitioner can do his day to day work. 14. Further, the Doctor who is the District Family Welfare Officer at Tumakuru and who treated the petitioner, is examined as PW.4 and she has produced Ex.P.25 copy of face page and the MLC extract, Hence, petitioner is entitled for total medical expenses of Rs.17,81,063/-. As per the evidence of PW.3 doctor, the petitioner need another surgery for removal of IM nailing in tibia and the estimated cost for the above surgery is at Rs.75,000/-. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:- Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs. 1. Loss of future income 2,87,100-00 2. Pain and Sufferings 40,000-00 3 . Attendant charges, extra 40,000-00 nutritious food and conveyance charges 4. Medical Expenses 17,81,063-00 5. Loss of future amenities and 40,000-00 unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid up 58,000-00 period 7. Future medical expenses 40,000-00 Total 22,86,163-00 28. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.22,86,163/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.
texts.arguments: 34. The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the following citations in support of case of the petitioner:- (SCCH-3) 28 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 Civil Appeal No.12046/2017 in a case of Kavita Nagar and others V/s The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein it is held that the addition of future prospects cannot Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/ 11 be denied in cases of self-employed persons or those employed on a fixed salary. 35. Further, the counsel for the respondent No.1 has relied upon the following citations in support of its contention:- 01. ILR 2002 KAR 893 in a case of Kumari Jyothi and others V/s Mohd. Usman Ali and others, wherein it is held that, "Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (Central Act No.59 of 1988) Sections 122, 166 and 168 - Accident occurred about one hour after midnight when a Motor Cycle driven by the deceased crashed into an unattended Lorry parked without any sign or indication to warn the other road users and in this accident both the Motor Cycle driver and pillion rider died. Tribunal apportioned negligence equally between the driver of the Motor Cycle and the driver of the Lorry. In appeal (SCCH-3) 29 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 High Court held that the negligence could be attributed only to the driver of the Lorry in view of the provision of Sec.122 of the Act. Sec.122 of the Motor Vehicles Act. 1988 provides that no person in-charge of a motor vehicle shall cause or allow the vehicle to be abandoned or to remain at rest on any public place in such a position or in such a condition or in such circumstances as to cause or likely to cause danger. obstruction or undue inconvenience to other users of the public place or to the passengers. the High Court of Gujarat in Premlata Nilamchand Sharma V/s Hirabhai Ranchhodbhai Patel, the High Court of Punjab and Haryana in Nirmal Bhutani V/s Haryana State and the Delhi High Court in Pushpa Rani Chopra V/s Anokha Singh have held that where the place was dark and where the vehicle was parked without any sign or indication to warn other road users, the negligence is on the driver of the parked vehicle and (SCCH-3) 30 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 not the driver of any vehicle which dashes into such parked vehicle. We are thus satisfied that the driver of the parked lorry was alone to be blamed as he had parked the lorry in the middle of the road without any sign or indications for other road users. (para 14) 02. ILR 2014 KAR 2558 in a case of Devaraju.T V/s The United India Insurance Company Ltd., rep. by its Manager, Bangalore and another, wherein it is held that, (a) The question of contributory negligence arises when there has been some act or omission on the claimant's part, which has materiallv contributed to the damage caused, and is of such a nature that it may properly be described as 'negligence'. The expression 'contributory negligence' means the failure by a person to use reasonable care for the safety of either himself or his property, so that he Malleshappa vs K.S.R.T.C on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33214437/ 12 becomes blameworthy in part as an author of his own wrong. It is well settled that where, by his negligence, if one (SCCH-3) 31 M.V.C.No.5337/2021 party places another in a situation of danger, which compels, other to act quickly in order to extricate himself, it does not amount to contributory negligence if that other acts in a way. (Para 15)
